data.title: Blue Shield says it shared health info on up to 4.7M patients with Google Ads
data.author: LinuxBender
data.article_summary: 美国健康保险公司Blue Shield of California在未经约470万会员知情或同意的情况下，将他们的健康信息分享给了Google的广告系统。这些信息可能包括医疗理赔日期、就诊机构、姓名、保险计划详情、居住城市及邮编、性别、家庭规模、账户标识符、财务责任信息，以及使用“找医生”工具时的搜索查询和结果。该数据通过Google Analytics被错误地传递给了Google Ads，可能被用于定向广告。Blue Shield声称已在2024年1月切断连接，并表示没有证据显示这些信息被用于其他目的或与第三方共享。此事件被视为违反HIPAA合规要求。Google则表示，企业应对数据管理负责，并声称其政策禁止收集和使用敏感健康信息。

Blue Shield says it shared health info on up to 4.7M patients with Google Ads
21
Tech giants don't need smartphone mics to target adverts – your insurer just gives your data away, anyway
Jessica Lyons
Wed 23 Apr 2025
//
22:18 UTC
US health insurance giant Blue Shield of California handed sensitive health information belonging to as many as 4.7 million members to Google's advertising empire, likely without these individuals' knowledge or consent.
The
data shared
may have included medical claim dates and providers used, which raises the specter of Google targeting ads based on the fact that you booked an appointment with a certain type of doctor - say, a cancer specialist, fertility clinic, or psychiatrist.
Other info potentially shared with Google ranged from patient names, insurance plan details, city of residence and zip code, gender, family size, and Blue Shield-assigned account identifiers, to financial responsibility info, and search queries and results for the "Find a Doctor" tool — including location, plan type, and provider details.
Exactly what was shared depended on what healthcare you were receiving, and whether you accessed or entered your info into Blue Shield's websites between 2021 and 2024, from what we can tell.
Blue Shield gave this info to Google via its visitor analysis tool, and the web giant may have used that data to target individuals with tailored ads, according to a privacy breach notification sent this month by Blue Shield to
4.7 million people
potentially caught up in this blunder.
As we understand it, Blue Shield embedded into its webpages code that would send visitor data to Google Analytics, a suite of tools for monitoring and measuring website users. In turn, these logs were passed to Google Ads due to a configuration fumble by the insurer.
"Like other health plans," Blue Shield previously used Google Analytics to track how members interact with its websites and which sites they visit, the insurance company admitted. The outfit claims this was all "to improve the services we provide to our members."
That health info did not necessarily remain between the insurer and its members, however.
Google may have used this data to conduct focused ad campaigns back to those individual members
"On February 11, 2025, Blue Shield discovered that, between April 2021 and January 2024, Google Analytics was configured in a way that allowed certain member data to be shared with Google's advertising product, Google Ads, that likely included protected health information," according to an April 9 notice on the insurance goliath's website.
"Google may have used this data to conduct focused ad campaigns back to those individual members," the note continued. "We want to reassure our members that no bad actor was involved, and, to our knowledge, Google has not used the information for any purpose other than these ads or shared the protected information with anyone."
You might have noted the uncertainty in Blue Shield's statements, which it blames on the "complexity and scope of the disclosures," saying "Blue Shield is unable to confirm whether any particular member's specific information was affected."
Blue Shield says it "severed" the connection between Google Analytics and Google Ads on its websites in January 2024, and has "no reason to believe" that any member data has been shared since.
"Upon discovering the issue, Blue Shield immediately initiated a review of its websites and security protocols to ensure that no other analytics tracking software is impermissibly sharing members' protected health information," the insurer noted.

How I made $64k from deleted files — a bug bounty story
Sharon Brizinov

TL;DR
— I built an automation that cloned and scanned tens of thousands of public GitHub repos for leaked secrets. For each repository I restored deleted files, found dangling blobs and unpacked
.pack
files to search in them for exposed API keys, tokens, and credentials. Ended up reporting a bunch of leaks and pulled in around $64k from bug bounties 🔥.
Outline
Background
Git internals
Collecting Targets
Building the Automation
Findings & Payments
Summary
Background
My name is
Sharon Brizinov
, and while I usually focus on low-level vulnerability and exploitation research in OT/IoT devices, I occasionally dive into bug bounty hunting.
Many researchers in the bugbounty space look for leaked secrets, often scanning GitHub repositories for exposed credentials. This approach isn’t new, but I wanted to explore a different angle-recovering secrets from allegedly deleted files. Developers often forget that Git history retains everything, even after files are removed from the working directory.
To test this, I scanned tens of thousands of repositories from thousands of companies, searching for sensitive information hidden in past commits. The results were alarming-I discovered numerous deleted files containing API tokens, credentials, and even active session tokens that had not been revoked. Reporting these findings led to significant security improvements for the affected companies, and in the end, I earned a total of $64,350 in bug bounty rewards.
In this blog I will try to describe my journey from collecting all the Github repositories, building the automation, and finding & reporting on leaking secrets.
Git internals
First thing first, I highly recommend reading
How git Internally works
by Octobot. It’s a great easy-to-read resource to understand better git.
Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes in files and allows multiple developers to collaborate on a project. It maintains a complete history of all changes, enabling users to revert to previous states, branch off for feature development, and merge changes efficiently. At its core, Git operates as a content-addressable filesystem where each version of a file is stored as a unique object in a repository.
Everything Git tracks (files, folders, commits, etc.) is stored as an
object
, identified by its
SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash
(depending on config).
There are four object types in Git:
Blob
→ File content
Tree
→ Directory structure
Commit
→ Snapshot + metadata
Tag
→ Annotated tag object
Git Blobs and Packs
A
blob
(binary large object) is how Git stores the
content of a file
,
without any filename or path info
. When Git first stores an object, it writes it as a “
loose object”
, like this:
.git/objects/ab/cdef1234567890...
Where
ab
is the first 2 hex characters of the SHA and
cdef1234567890…
is the rest. The binary data stored inside is a zlib-compressed data that corresponds to a single file.
To optimize storage and performance, Git periodically (loose objects ≥ 6700 by defualt) compresses many loose objects into a pack file:
.git/objects/pack/pack-<hash>.pack
.pack
files are complex beasts with very
interesting structure
. Luckily we don’t really need to fully understand how it is constructed, since we can use
git-unpack-objects
to unpack any
.pack
file.
How to identify pack and blob files: 50 41 43 4B — PACK | 78 01 — start of a zlib compressed blob (images taken using
HexShare
)
Sometimes unreferenced objects (aka dangling objects) will be created in our git repository. These are valid but unreferenced objects (commits, blobs, trees, or tags) that remain in the
.git/objects/
directory but are no longer reachable from any branch, tag, stash, or reflog. They are typically created when history is rewritten (for example by doing
git commit --amend
,
rebase
,
reset
, or branch deletion), leaving old objects behind. Although not part of the active history, Git retains them temporarily (by default, 2 weeks) for potential recovery. You can find them using
git fsck --dangling
Git Commit History
Each commit in Git represents a snapshot of the repository at a given point in time. Commits are immutable and are identified by a SHA-1/SHA-256 hash. They store:
A reference to a tree object, which represents the file structure at that commit.
Pointers to parent commits, forming a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of repository history.
Metadata, including the author, timestamp, and commit message.
Git stores commits efficiently using delta compression, meaning it only records changes rather than full copies of files.
Commit — tree — blob relationship (Image taken from
here
)
Deleted Files and Why They Can Be Recovered
When a file is deleted using
git rm
or simply removed from the working directory and committed, it disappears from the latest snapshot but still exists in the repository’s history. This happens because:

data.title: Hooded pitohui, one of the only toxic birds
data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: The hooded pitohui, found in Papua New Guinea, is one of the world's only known toxic birds. Its feathers contain batrachotoxins, potent neurotoxic alkaloids also found in South America's poison dart frogs. Ornithologist Jack Dumbacher discovered this in 1989 when handling the birds caused his hands to tingle and his mouth to burn. Later research revealed that the toxin comes from the pitohui's diet of melyrid beetles. Why this bird consumes such toxic prey, despite having other defenses, remains a mystery. This trait is rare among birds, making the hooded pitohui a unique case in the animal kingdom.

Hooded pitohui, one of the world’s only toxic birds
Hooded pitohui, one of the world’s only toxic birds
Contributor
Bec Crew
Contributor
Bec Crew
Bec Crew is a Sydney-based science communicator with a love for weird and wonderful animals. From strange behaviours and special adaptations to newly discovered species and the researchers who find them, her topics celebrate how alien yet relatable so many of the creatures that live amongst us can be.
By Bec Crew
•
12 June 2014
The hooded pitohui has toxic feathers.
Image credit: Jack Dumbacher
Reading Time:
2
Minutes
•
Print this page
This is one of the only known birds to be toxic. Its feathers contain one of the most potent toxins known to science – but why?
EXPLORING THE MISSISSIPPI River with his hunting dog, Dash, some time in the early 1800s, artist and ornithologist John James Audubon decided to perform a little experiment.
According to the native Americans and some scattered literary references, the beautiful green and gold Carolina parakeets that once littered the south-eastern United States were deadly toxic, and John had to know for sure. So he caught some by the side of the river, boiled them up and fed them to his dog to see what happened.
Was Dash okay? No one knows, but all mention of her in John’s well-kept diary stops dead at this Mississippi meal, so perhaps her fate was sealed when she fed on what could have been the only species of toxic bird in the world.
Sadly, the Carolina parakeet has been extinct for almost a century, but another toxic bird lives on. In 1989, Jack Dumbacher from the California Academy of Sciences travelled to the Papua New Guinea bush in search of birds of paradise.
Toxic hooded pitohui found in PNG
He strung up a number of delicate nets between the trees, and one day found several striking songbirds tangled in them. They were hooded pitohuis (
Pitohui dichrous
), little black and orange passerines with powerful beaks and dark red eyes.
As Jack struggled to free the pitohuis from his nets, they scratched his hands and the cuts hurt more than they should have. He put his fingers in his mouth to dull the pain, but that only made his tongue tingle and burn.
When Jack asked the locals if they knew anything about this peculiar effect, they knew all too well to stay away from the hooded pitohui – “a rubbish bird”, they said; no good for eating.
Jack flew some pitohui feathers back to the US for further testing, and showed them to chemist John Daly at the National Institute of Health. Years earlier, Daly had identified the presence of batrachotoxins – extremely potent neurotoxic steroidal alkaloids that in high doses can lead to paralysis, cardiac arrest and death – in the tiny poison dart frogs of South America.
Why is the hooded pitohui toxic?
Gram for gram, it is one of the most toxic natural substances known to science. In 1992, Daly found that exact same toxin in the feather fibres of the hooded pitohui.
Twelve years later, with the help of the Papua New Guinea locals, Jack discovered that the pitohuis were getting their batrachotoxins from the small melyrid beetles they fed on.
It was a mystery solved, but what drove these birds to pick the highly toxic melyrids as their primary food source? A tiny, defenceless dart frog needs all the help it can get, but a free-flying bird with claws and a powerful beak? Why the hooded pitohui ended up toxic is anyone’s guess.

data.title: Review: Ryzen AI CPU makes the Framework Laptop 13 the fastest has ever been
data.author: freeqaz
data.article_summary: The Framework Laptop 13 is a familiar, repairable, and upgradeable device, now featuring the Ryzen AI 300 series. This update offers significant CPU and GPU performance boosts, particularly with the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 chip, improving speed but reducing battery life. The Ryzen AI 300 version starts at $1,099 for pre-built models and $899 for DIY versions, with a high-end option costing $1,659. It meets Microsoft’s Copilot+ PC requirements, providing locally processed AI features. Externally, new colorful translucent accessories are available, and the keyboard has minor improvements, including a tweaked key structure and new legends, though these changes aren’t essential for current users. Overall, it’s the fastest Framework Laptop yet, with some trade-offs in battery life.

At this point, the Framework Laptop 13 is a familiar face, an old friend. We have
reviewed
this
laptop
five
other times
, and in that time, the idea of a repairable and upgradeable laptop has gone from a "sounds great if they can pull it off" idea to one that's become pretty reliable and predictable. And nearly four years out from the original version—which shipped with an
11th-generation Intel Core processor
—we're at the point where an upgrade will get you significant boosts to CPU and GPU performance, plus some other things.
We're looking at
the Ryzen AI 300 version
of the Framework Laptop today, currently available for preorder and shipping in Q2 for people who buy one now. The laptop starts at $1,099 for a pre-built version and $899 for a RAM-less, SSD-less, Windows-less DIY version, and we've tested the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 version that starts at $1,659 before you add RAM, an SSD, or an OS.
This board is a direct upgrade to Framework's Ryzen 7040-series board from mid-2023, with most of the same performance benefits we saw last year
when we first took a look at the Ryzen AI 300 series
. It's also, if this matters to you, the first Framework Laptop to meet Microsoft's requirements for its Copilot+ PC initiative, giving users access to some extra locally processed AI features (including but not limited to Recall) with the promise of more to come.
For this upgrade, Ryzen AI giveth, and Ryzen AI taketh away. This is the fastest the Framework Laptop 13 has ever been (at least, if you spring for the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 chip that our review unit shipped with). If you're looking to do some light gaming (or non-Nvidia GPU-accelerated computing), the Radeon 890M GPU is about as good as it gets. But you'll pay for it in battery life—never a particularly strong point for Framework, and less so here than in most of the Intel versions.
What’s new, Framework?
This Framework update brings the return of colorful translucent accessories, parts you can also add to an older Framework Laptop if you want.
Credit:
Andrew Cunningham
We're going to focus on what makes this particular Framework Laptop 13 different from the past iterations. We talk more about the build process and the internals in
our review of the 12th-generation Intel Core version
, and we ran lots of battery tests with the new screen in our review of the
Intel Core Ultra version
. We also have coverage of
the original Ryzen version of the laptop
, with the Ryzen 7 7840U and Radeon 780M GPU installed.
Per usual, every internal refresh of the Framework Laptop 13 comes with another slate of external parts. Functionally, there's not a ton of exciting stuff this time around—certainly nothing as interesting as the higher-resolution 120 Hz screen option we got with last year's Intel Meteor Lake update—but there's a handful of things worth paying attention to.
Functionally, Framework has slightly improved the keyboard, with "a new key structure" on the spacebar and shift keys that "reduce buzzing when your speakers are cranked up." I can't really discern a difference in the feel of the keyboard, so this isn't a part I'd run out to add to my own Framework Laptop, but it's a fringe benefit if you're buying an all-new laptop or replacing your keyboard for some other reason.
Keyboard legends have also been tweaked; pre-built Windows versions get Microsoft's dedicated (and, within limits, customizable) Copilot key, while DIY editions come with a Framework logo on the Windows/Super key (instead of the word "super") and no Copilot key.

data.title: How a 20 year old bug in GTA San Andreas surfaced in Windows 11 24H2
data.author: yett
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了在Windows 11 24H2更新后，《GTA: San Andreas》游戏中的Skimmer水上飞机消失的bug。玩家报告称，无论是否使用模组或SilentPatch，Skimmer都无法生成，且尝试生成时游戏可能会冻结。经过调查，发现问题源于游戏代码中处理旋翼角度的循环，因浮点数运算错误导致旋翼速度异常高，最终引发bug。该问题仅在Windows 11 24H2版本中出现，推测是该系统更新引发的API问题。SilentPatch在一定程度上减轻了问题，但未完全解决。

I might have been skeptical if someone had told me years ago that
C#
would become my programming language of choice for most projects. Like many developers, I've explored various languages throughout my career—from low-level C++ to the enterprise king Java. Yet I keep returning to C#, and many people ask me why.
C#
was Microsoft's answer to Java during the platform wars of the early 2000s, but it quickly became something Java never could. It was designed as a strongly typed language that combined the robustness of C++ with the simplicity of Visual Basic.
Unlike some languages that struggle to evolve, C# has been continuously refined, adapting to modern programming paradigms, yet it has maintained backward compatibility.
Some people often ask me why I chose C# instead of many other languages, and in this text, I will try to explain why.
C# Timeline from C# 1.0 to C# 13.0
We will discuss the following:
What is C#?
An overview of C#'s origins, goals, core characteristics, and design philosophy.
The language
. We will discuss essential C# features, including Object-oriented programming, the type system, generics, lambdas, LINQ, async/await, and memory management.
The .NET ecosystem.
We will explore the ecosystem where C# lives, its different runtimes, and the frameworks that enable it to target various application domains.
Tooling
. We will check popular development tools and IDEs such as Visual Studio, Visual Studio Code, JetBrains Rider, and the .NET CLI.
Libraries
. We will explore he standard .NET libraries and popular third-party packages available via NuGet.
Documentation
. What are some available and popular resources, official documentation, and recommended materials for learning C# and .NET.
Community
. We will answer the questions about what kind of community C# has and the critical initiatives, resources, and platforms that support developers.
The popularity contest
. We will check how popular C# is, its rankings, relevance to the job market, salaries, and community perception.
C# vs other languages
. How C# compares to Java, Python, F#, and JavaScript/TypeScript.
The future of C#.
What is the future evolution of C#, recent language advancements, and Microsoft's vision for continued innovation.
Conclusion
. My insights on why C# is a good choice and suitable for various development scenarios.
Bonus: A brief history of C#
.
A historical timeline highlighting significant milestones in the evolution of the C# language.
So, let’s dive in.

Uno Platform
gives you:
🧰 A complete open-source engine for cross-platform development

🧭 Prebuilt extensions for DI, navigation, and reactive programming, and more
🎨 A powerful WYSIWYG designer — edit your live running app 🤯
🛠️ Works with Visual Studio, VS Code, and Rider
Start building today
1. What is C#?
C#
(pronounced "C-sharp") is a modern, multi-paradigm programming language developed by Microsoft. Created by
Anders Hejlsberg
and his team as part of the .NET initiative (he leads TypeScript today), C# was designed from the ground up to be object-oriented, component-oriented, and type-safe.
💡
The name itself has an interesting origin
—it's a musical reference.
The '#' symbol indicates that a semitone should raise a note in musical notation. So, "C#" suggests that the language is an
"increment" over C/C++
. The # symbol also cleverly resembles four "+" signs stacked together, hinting at C# being "C++++."
When C# was first released, a simple "Hello World" program required several lines of code with namespaces, classes, and method declarations. But as the language evolved, it became simpler. With C# 9's top-level statements, the simplest C# program can now be written as:
Isn’t this great? A cross-platform super-rich language can have a one-liner program.
At its core, C# is:
Modern
: Continuously updated with new features that reflect the evolving programming landscape
Mature
: It is 25 years old and has significantly evolved, but it is still active in development.
Type-safe
: Prevents type errors through its strong type system.
Multi-paradigm
: It is a strongly object-oriented language, which includes imperative, declarative, and functional programming styles.
Component-oriented
: Supports the development of self-contained, reusable components.
Cross-platform
: Although initially reserved for Windows, it can now run on Linux, Mac, and other platforms.
Versatile
: Suitable for developing a wide range of applications from web to mobile to desktop
Open-source:
Since version 7, C # has been fully developed openly on GitHub, and Microsoft accepts feedback and proposals from the community on the

data.title: OpenVSX, which VSCode forks rely on for extensions, down for 24 hours
data.author: aaronvg
data.article_summary: 截至2025年4月24日，官方主页、查询API、搜索API和VSCode资产API等服务因后端存储问题导致宕机，正在努力修复。该问题从4月23日11:31am EDT开始，目前仍在解决中。此前已有4次更新记录，显示持续处理该事故。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源项目和开发工具的现状，特别是关于去中心化与中心化托管的争议，以及对VSCode及其替代品的讨论。

不同观点：
• [0xbadcafebee] 认为过去开源项目通过多个随机镜像托管，去中心化的方式更加自由和可靠，而现在依赖大公司的免费服务，导致个人信息和数据的让渡。他主张改变现状，回归更简单的时代。
• [fr4nkr] 分享了使用VSCodium的负面体验，指出其对中心化仓库（OpenVSX）的依赖导致功能缺失，并对比了Emacs的手动安装简便性，认为VSCodium的努力是徒劳的。
• [joshstrange] 将VSCode比作Android，认为其开源版本（VSCodium）在没有市场和插件支持的情况下几乎不可用，批评微软的商业模式。
• [exceptione] 推荐Eclipse Theia作为VSCode的替代品，认为其完全开放且无“间谍软件”，同时批评微软的销售公司本质。
• [loloquwowndueo] 指出VSCode设计上就是为了“分裂”，其分支是其设计的一部分。
• [jamisonbryant] 讨论了GitLab对OpenVSX的支持，强调了扩展支持对开发团队的重要性。

补充讨论：
• [john-h-k] 提到了Helix编辑器，并推荐给那些寻找Vim/Emacs替代品的人。
• [gchamonlive] 推荐了Lazy Vim，并分享了其易用性和配置经验。
• [khimaros] 提到了Lapce编辑器，认为其是该领域的一个有趣竞争者。
• [mdaniel] 提供了关于Eclipse Foundation服务中断的技术细节，强调了中心化托管的潜在问题。
• [jononor] 寻求现代、开箱即用、支持多种开发领域的开源IDE替代品。
• [thomond] 建议手动下载和安装扩展，以解决中心化托管服务中断的问题。
• [Dwedit] 提出使用IPFS/IPNS作为去中心化备份方案。
• [Havoc] 分享了学习neovim的经验，认为其避免了VSCode对Remote SSH扩展的依赖。
• [throwaway42167] 指出可以配置VSCodium使用微软的扩展库，并通过一些技巧使其兼容VSCode插件，但由于法律原因无法开箱即用。

争议焦点：
• 中心化托管（如VSCode和其插件市场）的可靠性与去中心化托管的对比。
• 开源项目对大公司免费服务的依赖是否会导致个人数据和隐私的让渡。
• VSCode及其开源替代品（如VSCodium和Eclipse Theia）在功能和易用性上的差异。

data.title: OpenAI releases image generation in the API
data.author: themanmaran
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI图像生成API的应用、价格、质量及其在不同场景中的使用

不同观点：
• [cuuupid] 提到政府和军方相关任务的拒绝率很高，可能会促使承包商使用中国开发的开源模型，从而带来安全风险。同时，提到有几乎无内容审核的API访问层，但不清楚如何申请该层级，且已有一些国防承包商在使用。
• [tezza] 分享了使用不同质量类型生成图像的实验，并提供了生成结果的比较链接。
• [Imnimo] 对需要大量生成图像的应用场景表示好奇，质疑是否真的有这种需求，因为个人使用通常是一次性的。
• [jeevships] 对从GPT图像包装器购买生成图像服务的必要性提出疑问，认为用户可以直接在GPT中生成。
• [film42] 分享了在平台上生成图像的费用体验，认为对于面向客户的产品而言，费用过高。
• [minimaxir] 对API的定价和图像质量进行了详细分析，指出其生成速度和质量不如竞争对手，且提示方法更为复杂。
• [badmonster] 提供了关于GPT图像API定价的详细信息，认为对于初创公司来说费用较高。
• [gervwyk] 希望有能够生成可编辑SVG图像的AI工具，目前AI生成的图像不符合品牌要求，认为Canva是最好的工具。
• [claiir] 提到GoDaddy正在尝试整合图像生成技术，以便客户轻松创建可编辑的Logo，并提到过去的一个定制图像生成模型项目可能被GPT图像模型取代。
• [jumploops] 指出新模型基于自回归（类似于LLM，逐token生成），相比扩散模型更能准确遵循文本提示，并分享了实际使用中的成功案例。
• [verelo] 提到一个视频编辑平台整合了GPT图像模型以改进文本生成和编辑控制，质疑这是否意味着该模型也能处理视频。
• [sebastiennight] 对当前从参考图像和提示生成高清图像的API状态和价格提出疑问，希望找到更经济的方案。
• [greatgib] 对图像token的定价单位表示不解，希望了解具体如何计算。
• [jonplackett] 询问是否可以同时输入图像和文本以生成新图像，认为这是新图像模型最强大的使用方式，但目前似乎不支持。
• [gcrfelix] 总结教训：永远不要围绕优化现有AI能力来构建竞争优势。

补充讨论：
• 关于图像生成API的定价和质量的讨论较多，尤其是与竞争对手的比较。
• 用户对API的具体使用方法和应用场景存在疑问，特别是如何更有效地结合图像和文本输入。
• 有用户关注如何生成特定格式（如SVG）的图像，并对其编辑功能提出要求。
• 对图像生成在商业和专业领域（如Logo设计、视频编辑）的潜在应用进行了探讨。

争议焦点：
• 图像生成API的定价是否过高，特别是对于初创公司和需要大量生成图像的用户。
• 新模型的图像生成质量和速度是否优于或劣于其他竞争对手。
• 是否应该或如何围绕现有AI能力构建竞争优势。

data.title: Show HN: I reverse engineered top websites to build an animated UI library
data.author: armedin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一套从优秀网站逆向工程而来的UI组件库，提供多种潮流动画组件，方便集成到项目中，且已预设好样式和动画。目前有数十种组件可供浏览，包括Logo Dots、Bot Protection、Glowing Orb、SMS Alert等，涵盖了交互、安全、界面美化等功能。用户可以以50美元的优惠价获得终身访问权。部分组件如Role-Based Access Control、Multifactor Authentication、AI Chat等将在2024至2025年间推出。价格优惠仅限时提供。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对UI组件网站的评价与争议

不同观点：
• [正面评价]
  - 赞赏分享和社区贡献：toddmorey（对学习和分享的肯定），zacksiri（对设计和技术的赞赏），ajjenkins（愿意为实用组件付费）
  - 对设计和功能的喜爱：zacksiri（对动画和框架的满意），caseyy（喜欢特定组件设计）

• [负面评价与争议]
  - 对商业行为的质疑：toddmorey（对克隆组件收费的反感），jwilber（对利用AI重现和销售他人工作的反感）
  - 用户体验问题：kmoser（图标功能不明确），naavis（网站加载对硬件要求高），mediumsmart（动画导致的性能问题）

• [功能与技术细节]
  - 要求更多实现细节：ziftface（希望了解组件的可修改性和主题模式）
  - 兼容性问题：morteify（组件在Safari中显示错误）

• [设计与动画]
  - 对动画的批评：Fokamul（认为无动画的网页更好），hexo（认为动画是障碍）

补充讨论：
• 暗黑模式的批评：Mystery-Machine（指出通过误导性按钮诱导付费是暗黑模式）
• 设计灵感：PStamatiou（指出网站设计受到Rauno启发，甚至有相似按钮）

争议焦点：
• 是否应通过付费获取组件代码，以及获取过程中的透明性和公平性（Mystery-Machine提出的暗黑模式问题）
• 利用AI技术重现和销售组件的道德性与合法性（jwilber的观点）

总体来看，讨论主要围绕设计美学、用户体验、技术实现和商业行为的伦理问题展开。

data.title: PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为PyGraph的方法，旨在为PyTorch提供对CUDA Graphs的强大编译器支持。CUDA Graphs旨在通过捕捉和启动一系列GPU任务来减少CPU开销，但由于其静态结构和数据复制开销，实际部署中往往导致性能下降。PyGraph通过三项关键优化解决这些问题：扩大CUDA Graphs的适用范围、减少GPU内核参数复制开销、基于成本效益分析选择性部署CUDA Graphs。PyGraph无缝集成到PyTorch2的编译工具链中，无需手动修改代码即可提升性能。实验表明，PyGraph在多种机器学习基准测试中显著提升了性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python包命名、可复现性与实用性、技术实现细节与优化、对相关研究和机构的认可、源代码的缺失

不同观点：
• damnitbuilds认为该Python包用于CUDA Graphs，因此建议命名为"PyCudaGraph"更为合适，而不是"PyGraph"，以避免与其他类型的Python图形库混淆。

• infocollector指出，由于缺乏可直接通过pip安装的软件包（如"pip install pygraph"），难以全面评估该工作的可复现性和实际应用性。

• saagarjha对该技术表示赞赏，但希望看到其整合到PyTorch中，而不仅仅是一篇论文。他讨论了技术细节，指出图形中"bake-in"参数的问题，并建议通过间接引用指针来解决，同时提到这种方法可能带来的开销和信息丢失问题。他还提出未来可以探索在PyTorch中更好地支持CUDA图形，如条件节点。

• tho423i43234对印度科学学院（IISc）的研究工作表示认可，并提到相关研究人员和机构，如Pluto框架和PolyMage Labs，以及IISc的ArtPARK initiative，显示出对学术和产业结合的支持。

Computer Science > Machine Learning

Title:
PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch
Authors:
Abhishek Ghosh
,
Ajay Nayak
,
Ashish Panwar
,
Arkaprava Basu
View a PDF of the paper titled PyGraph: Robust Compiler Support for CUDA Graphs in PyTorch, by Abhishek Ghosh and 3 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
CUDA Graphs -- a recent hardware feature introduced for NVIDIA GPUs -- aim to reduce CPU launch overhead by capturing and launching a series of GPU tasks (kernels) as a DAG. However, deploying CUDA Graphs faces several challenges today due to the static structure of a graph. It also incurs performance overhead due to data copy. In fact, we show a counter-intuitive result -- deploying CUDA Graphs hurts performance in many cases.
We introduce PyGraph, a novel approach to automatically harness the power of CUDA Graphs within PyTorch2. Driven by three key observations, PyGraph embodies three novel optimizations: it enables wider deployment of CUDA Graphs, reduces GPU kernel parameter copy overheads, and selectively deploys CUDA Graphs based on a cost-benefit analysis. PyGraph seamlessly integrates with PyTorch2's compilation toolchain, enabling efficient use of CUDA Graphs without manual modifications to the code. We evaluate PyGraph across various machine learning benchmarks, demonstrating substantial performance improvements over PyTorch2.

data.title: Acquisitions, consolidation, and innovation in AI
data.author: pfarago
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大语言模型（LLM）技术的创新、应用和商业化前景

不同观点：
• no_wizard认为，模型创新正在趋同和放缓，大公司之间的模型质量差距缩小，技术逐渐商品化。未来竞争将集中在模型速度和准确性上，但单靠提供LLM模型本身难以获得巨大商业回报，真正的价值在于在技术上构建产品。他还质疑文章中关于企业不会围绕AI重组的观点，认为一些公司已经在进行重组以减少人力。
• lemax指出，最具竞争力的基础模型公司同时也是创新的应用构建者，例如Anthropic和OpenAI通过超级应用（如ChatGPT、Claude）吸引消费者，这些应用功能多样且战略重要。随着这些应用能力增强，它们将进一步商品化，并带动相关服务的发展。
• nc认为文章低估了OpenAI作为应用层公司的能力，指出OpenAI通过创新模型构建了原始的ChatGPT应用，并在用户体验上表现出色，有潜力在常见应用领域占据主导地位。
• stuart_real提到，像VSCode-based GPT-wrapper这样的项目获得高额投资，显示出LLM公司的迫切需求，Anthropic和xAI等公司也会通过收购增加其token使用。
• xnx认为，将前沿AI模型应用于特定业务领域的机会很多，成功与否更多取决于对业务领域的经验而非AI技术本身。AI初创公司仍有可能通过被大公司收购获得成功。
• blitzar以讽刺的口吻建议每个初创公司都应该生成一个简陋的AI包装产品，制造炒作，以吸引高额收购，认为这是当前气候下不负责任的行为。
• imoreno指出，收购不仅仅是为了获取初创公司的价值，有时是为了消除潜在竞争。大公司可能并不总是对增加更好的产品感兴趣，而是为了阻止竞争者发展更好的产品。他还认为，当前模型能力已经很好，应用创新才是关键。
• dismalaf认为，LLM领域对缺乏深厚财力者不友好，目前进入该领域无意义，因为它遇到了瓶颈。然而，寻找下一个AI范式仍有可能获得巨额回报。
• paulsutter则持乐观态度，认为当前是历史上最具影响力的时刻，是构建的最佳时机，鼓励学习和适应新工具。

补充讨论：
• 关于LLM技术是否已商品化及其未来创新潜力的争议是讨论的核心。no_wizard和imoreno认为技术已接近成熟，应用创新更为重要；而lemax和nc则强调基础模型公司的持续创新和应用潜力。
• 收购和竞争策略在讨论中被多次提及，imoreno和stuart_real指出收购有时是为了消除竞争，blitzar和xnx则强调在当前气候下通过收购获得成功的可能性。
• 关于AI技术对企业组织结构的影响也存在争议，no_wizard引用具体例子质疑文章观点，而其他评论者未深入探讨这一点。

data.title: A Tour Inside the IBM Z17
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了IBM z17主机的内部构造和主要技术规格。IBM于2025年4月8日发布了z17，该系统与前代z16一样，可安装在19英寸机架中，支持1到4个框架配置。在4框架版本中，最多可包含4个CPC抽屉、12个I/O抽屉以及两个散热组件。z17搭载了新的Telum II处理器，具备8个高性能核心，运行频率为5.5GHz，拥有40%的芯片缓存容量提升，并集成了新的AI加速器和低延迟数据处理单元（DPU）。其最大内存达到64TB，比前代有显著提升。此外，z17还引入了IBM Spyre加速器，专为AI工作负载设计，包含32个加速核心，采用5nm工艺技术。IBM z17的相关技术指南和红皮书已可供查阅，提供了详细的系统介绍和图解。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IBM Z系列大型主机及其相关技术、历史和应用

不同观点：
• [mrandish] 认为IBM Z系列保持与1964年发布的IBM 360的向后兼容性非常了不起，并强调了IBM 360在软件和硬件架构上的重大变革作用。他还指出，早期微型计算机的设计受到了360和DEC的PDP系列的影响。

• [strongpigeon] 提出疑问，当今谁在使用大型主机以及使用的目的，表现出对大型主机实际应用场景的不熟悉，并对比了传统硬件和云服务。

A Tour Inside the IBM z17
Like
Welcome to a photo-driven tour of the
IBM z17
. I've scoured the image library to pull dig deep inside these machines that most people don't get an opportunity to see inside, and I'll share some of the specifications gleaned from the announcement and related Redbooks.
On April 8th 2025 IBM announced the IBM z17 at the new One Madison Avenue headquarters. The fanfare of that event was followed by an
IBM Z Day Special Edition
which gave participants a deep look inside the new system hardware, along with the latest software innovations that will pair with it, including real world use cases by clients and partners. Replays are now available, and if you're reading this post and are particularly interested in hardware the
"Innovation up close: A sneak peak INSIDE a next generation mainframe"
session will be of particular interest to you, plus it's a real delight to watch.
But on with the blog post!
Fitting into a 19" rack space just like its predecessor, the IBM z16, the system already has the ability to fit into a familiar spot in the data center. The z17 features configurations spanning 1 to 4 frames.
Inside the 4-frame version you can have up to give 4 CPC drawers and 12 I/O drawers, and up to two RCAs (Radiator Cooling Assembly).
(Source: IBM z17 Technical Guide)
I was also impressed to learn that memory in a fully loaded system maxes out at 64T, up from 40T in its predecessor, which is quite the jump.
At the heart of the machine is the new IBM Telum II processor.
Telum II wafer, being held by yours truly!
I had the pleasure of attending Hot Chips back in August of 2024 where Chris Berry announced the features of this new processor, which includes:
A new AI accelerator with 4x the available compute power of the one included with the original IBM Telum processor
A new built-in low-latency data processing unit (DPU) for accelerated I/O
8 high-performance cores running at 5.5GHz
40% increase in on-chip cache capacity over Telum
(Source: IBM z17 Technical Guide)
One thing I want to call attention to is the DPU. Taken directly from the IBM z17 Technical Guide, section 3.4.7:
"The IBM z17 Data Processing Unit encompasses a comprehensive refactoring of the I/O subsystem. With the DPU, functionality from I/O Adapters' ASICs is moved into the Z CP chip."
That's pretty cool.
And all that memory and processors are packed into the lovely CPC drawer.
IBM z17 CPC Drawer
For a closer look, you can check out the
product page that includes Telum II
and the full announcement from IBM back in August of 2024:
"New Telum II Processor and IBM Spyre Accelerator: Expanding AI on IBM Z"
Which is the perfect segue into talking about the IBM Spyre Accelerator. In collaboration with the brilliant minds of IBM Research, this new AI accelerator is an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) specifically designed for AI workloads that’s the team at Research has dubbed an Artificial Intelligence Unit, or AIU.
It features:
32 individual accelerator cores
25.6 billion transistors using 14 miles of wire
5 nm node process technology
IBM Spyre Accelerator head on, chip exposed
It is mounted on a PCIe card for easy management, and can be clustered together with additional Spyre cards. If you're like me and curious about how we got there, IBM Research published a blog post about their work back in 2022 that gave a glimpse into their work with the original prototype that ultimately became Spyre in
"Meet the IBM Artificial Intelligence Unit"
, and in November of 2024 they shared some of what comes next in
"Charting a path to a more sustainable AI future"
. It's truly been a fascinating journey to watch, and now we're here!
The
IBM z17 Redbooks
are now available. Of particular interest will be the
IBM z17 Technical Introduction
and
IBM z17 (9175) Technical Guide
where many of the details for this blog post came from, and I think you'll find that the clearly marked diagrams throughout are a real treat. And many thanks to Kenny Stine for doing a technical review of this blog post before I let it out the door.

data.title: What Actually Happens at the End of 'Trading Places'? (2013)
data.author: austinallegro
data.article_summary: In the movie *Trading Places*, Louis Winthorpe and Billy Ray Valentine enact a plan to get rich by outsmarting the wealthy Duke brothers. The Dukes try to profit from insider information about the orange crop report, but Winthorpe and Valentine steal the real report and create a fake one. They trick the Dukes into believing the orange crop is bad, causing them to buy large amounts of orange juice futures, driving up the price. Winthorpe then sells futures contracts at a high price. When the true report is revealed, the price of orange juice plummets, and Winthorpe and Valentine buy back the contracts at a low price, making a huge profit. The Dukes, who bet wrong, lose everything. This scheme, based on trading commodities using government information, later inspired the "Eddie Murphy Rule," making such actions illegal.

Paramount/The Kobal Collection
It's been 30 years since
Trading Places
came out. And, to be honest, I never really understood what happened at the end of that movie. Sure, Louis Winthorpe (Dan Aykroyd) and Billy Ray Valentine (Eddie Murphy) get rich, and the Duke brothers lose all their money. But what actually happens? How does it work?
I recently talked to Tom Peronis, a guy who has spent years trading OJ options. He walked me through every step of Winthorpe and Valentine's plan.
1. Give The Duke Brothers Bad Information
The Duke brothers — two old, rich guys — have bribed someone to get an advance copy of a government report on the orange crop. This will give them inside information on what's going to happen in the market for frozen concentrated orange juice. But Winthorpe and Valentine find out what the Dukes are up to, and they manage to steal the crop report before the Duke brothers get it.
Sponsor Message
The report says the orange crop is strong. When the rest of the world learns this, the price of OJ will fall. So Winthorpe and Valentine create a fake crop report that they put into the hands of the Duke brothers. The fake crop report says the crop was bad. The Duke brothers see this, and believe the price of OJ will rise.
2. Drive Up The Price Of Orange Juice Futures
The setting, the floor of the commodities exchange. The Duke brothers have told their trader to buy orange juice futures, and to keep buying no matter how high the price goes.
The market opens, and the Duke brothers' trader starts buying. Everybody else sees this and thinks the Dukes know something. Suddenly, everybody's buying. The price goes up and up and up, and the Dukes keep buying.
3. Sell To The Suckers
Then comes the key line for the entire movie — a line that's almost unintelligible. Standing on the floor of the exchange, Winthorpe (Dan Aykroyd) yells out:
Sell 30 April at 142!
Here's what that means: He wants to promise to sell orange juice in April for $1.42 per pound. The "30" in his line means he wants to start by selling 30 contracts. (One contract = many, many pounds of OJ.) (Also, that "30" might be some other number. It's hard to understand what he's saying. But it doesn't really matter — they sell a lot of contracts.)
Sponsor Message
All the other traders think the price in April will be higher than $1.42. The traders mob Winthorpe and Valentine, agreeing to buy lots and lots of OJ from them at $1.42 a pound.
4. Wait For The Other Shoe To Drop
A minute later, everything on the trading floor goes quiet. Everybody looks at the TV. On the TV, the secretary of agriculture walks up to a podium and reads the orange crop report. The guy tells the world that the orange crop is fine.
5. Buy Low, Get Rich And Bankrupt Your Enemies
To the traders, this means that the price of OJ is not going to go through the roof. All those traders who, a minute ago, were buying all they could, now suddenly need to sell. So the price starts falling. When the price hits 29 cents a pound, Winthorpe and Valentine start agreeing to buy orange juice in April.
In other words, Winthorpe and Valentine have contracts allowing them to buy millions of pounds of orange juice in April for 29 cents a pound, and to sell it for $1.42 a pound. They sold high and bought low. They're rich. The Dukes made the opposite bet and went broke.
Bonus: The Eddie Murphy Rule
One interesting kicker to the story: Trading commodities on inside information obtained from the government wasn't actually illegal when the movie came out, but it's illegal now. It was banned in the 2010 finance-overhaul law, under a special provision often referred to as the
Eddie Murphy Rule
.
Note: This story was originally posted on July 12. It was updated on July 19 to add audio from the radio version.

data.title: Discord Indexes Trillions of Messages
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Discord如何处理和索引数万亿条消息，以及在系统扩展过程中遇到的问题和解决方案。起初，Discord使用Elasticsearch构建了消息搜索系统，通过将消息按服务器（guild）或直接消息（DM）分片存储，实现了高效、可扩展和易操作的搜索基础设施。然而，随着用户增长，系统出现了问题，包括Redis消息索引队列在Elasticsearch节点故障时丢弃消息，批量索引操作在节点故障时无法容错，以及大型Elasticsearch集群带来的性能和操作难度。此外，系统缺乏良好的软件升级路径，且面对极大 Guild 时索引大小受限。为解决这些问题，Discord需要优化索引系统，提高容错性，并支持更大规模的消息搜索。

• [JackSlateur] 讨论了Discord的技术架构变化，提到其从单一的Elasticsearch集群转向多个运行在Kubernetes上的Elasticsearch集群，并用GCP的PubSub替代了Redis。虽然这种设计听起来成本较高，但似乎是可行的技术方案。

补充讨论：
• [coldblues] 提供的链接（https://discordomicon.github.io/removal/overview/）指向了一份指南，详细介绍了如何尝试彻底删除Discord上的数据，表明用户在数据控制权上的被动性。
• [JackSlateur] 对Discord技术架构的评价表明，尽管设计上成本较高，但似乎是为了满足平台扩展性和性能需求，暗示了技术选择的合理性。

争议焦点：
• Discord在数据隐私和合规性方面的表现引发了对用户数据控制权和隐私保护的质疑，特别是用户删除数据的过程复杂且不透明。
• 技术架构的调整虽然看似昂贵，但其必要性和效果也成为讨论的一部分，尤其是从系统性能和可维护性角度的权衡。

43786374.article_content:
Engineering & Developers
How Discord Indexes Trillions of Messages
Vicki Niu
April 24, 2025
Back in 2017, we shared how we built our message search system to
index billions of messages
. We designed our search infrastructure to be performant, cost-effective, scalable, and easy to operate. We chose to use Elasticsearch, with Discord messages sharded over
indices
, the logical namespace for Elasticsearch messages, on two Elasticsearch clusters. Messages were sharded either by Discord server (which weâll refer to as a guild from here on out) or direct message (DM). This allowed us to store all a guildâs messages together for fast querying and run smaller, more manageable clusters. Since not everyone uses search, messages were lazily indexed into Discord, and we built a message queue that allowed workers to pull chunks of messages for indexing to leverage Elasticsearchâs bulk-indexing capabilities.
But as Discord grew, our search infrastructure began to exhibit a few cracksâ¦
â
Our Redis message indexing queue would drop messages
We used Redis to back our realtime message indexing queue, which held up great
at first
. However, when our indexing queue got backed up for any reason, which happened often on Elasticsearch node failure, the Redis cluster became a source of failure that began dropping messages once CPU maxed out with too many messages in the queue.
Our bulk indexing was fault-intolerant on Elasticsearch index or node failure
Part of the reason our indexing queue was so impacted by Elasticsearch node failures is because of how we optimized our bulk message indexing. The realtime index workers pulled batches of messages off the queue to index to Elasticsearch. However, these messages all belonged to different indices and Elasticsearch nodes in our cluster â one bulk index operation with a batch of 50 messages might then fan out to 50 Elasticsearch nodes in the cluster! If one operation in the batch fails, then the entire bulk index operation would be considered failed, re-enqueueing all messages to be retried.
To put it into perspective, let's say our Elasticsearch cluster had 100 nodes, and we were indexing batches of 50 messages. If one node fails, assuming an equal distribution, the odds of a given batch having at least one message going to that failed node are ~40%. This means that a
single-node
failure leads to ~40% of our bulk index operations failing!
Large Elasticsearch clusters had large overhead, impacting performance and operability
As our message volume grew, we scaled up our Elasticsearch clusters by adding additional nodes. This allowed us to horizontally-scale quite easily by adding more indices and nodes to serve more Discord servers and their messages. However, adding these also meant that each of our bulk index operations were now also spread across a much larger number of indices and nodes. Operations fanned out more, causing slowdown to our indexing performance. Additionally, the more nodes we have in a cluster, the more likely a cluster was to fail at any point.
No good path to software upgrades or rolling restarts
Given the systemâs lack of resilience to single node unavailability, we didn't have a good solution for performing rolling restarts and doing software upgrades. Our clusters had also grown really large and unwieldy, with over 200 nodes and terabytes of data total. Any strategy to gracefully drain nodes before restart to ensure service availability wouldâve taken a prohibitively long time. We were forced to keep our clusters running legacy OS versions and Elasticsearch versions, missing both critical updates and performance improvements.
Most notably, patching the
log4shell vulnerability
by disabling JNDI lookups and setting

43786374.article_summary: 本文介绍了Discord如何处理和索引数万亿条消息，以及在系统扩展过程中遇到的问题和解决方案。起初，Discord使用Elasticsearch构建了消息搜索系统，通过将消息按服务器（guild）或直接消息（DM）分片存储，实现了高效、可扩展和易操作的搜索基础设施。然而，随着用户增长，系统出现了问题，包括Redis消息索引队列在Elasticsearch节点故障时丢弃消息，批量索引操作在节点故障时无法容错，以及大型Elasticsearch集群带来的性能和操作难度。此外，系统缺乏良好的软件升级路径，且面对极大 Guild 时索引大小受限。为解决这些问题，Discord需要优化索引系统，提高容错性，并支持更大规模的消息搜索。

data.author: petekoomen
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI功能在实际应用中的价值和问题

不同观点：
• joshstrange：认为90%的AI功能是附加且无用的，尤其是价格过高。除了一些编码工具（如Copilot、Claude Code），其他AI功能（如Gmail的AI重写邮件功能）并没有实际提升用户体验。用户更倾向于直接使用Claude或ChatGPT来完成任务。
• tlogan：指出AI无法解决用户不清楚自己目标的问题，反而可能放大这种模糊性。AI可以降低新工具的学习曲线，但也可能阻碍用户深入思考和掌握技能。当前很多AI功能的添加是盲目的，没有真正考虑用户需求。
• mNovak：认为AI工具（如LLM）可以被调优以产生更人性化的结果，但大公司可能故意加入一些 uncanny valley 效果以避免用户不安。
• crote：提出最有用的AI功能往往不被注意，比如邮件标签助手。这些功能虽然提供实际价值，但由于不够显眼，无法吸引用户注意。
• throwaway2037：引用Joel Spolsky的博客，认为AI在某些情况下像是一个低效的员工，增加了工作时间而非减少。
• imoreno：认为用户没有充分利用LLM，并且指出AI在处理高精度任务（如数学计算）时表现不佳是正常的，因为这不是它的设计目的。同时批评了将AI视为商业模式转变核心的观点。
• selkin：分享了自己使用统计模型分类和回复邮件的经验，认为AI使得这些功能更易于实现，而无需用户具备编程技能。
• kristjank：对使用AI撰写消息持怀疑态度，认为AI缺乏个性化表达，且可能带来数据隐私问题。
• benterris：认为AI撰写消息缺乏个人表达的意义，尤其在与亲密人士交流时。
• Karrot_Kream：指出很多AI功能的添加是为了追逐市场热点，而非真正满足用户需求。
• kkoncevicius：认为AI功能最终可能完全消除人类之间的互动，例如自动生成和审核邮件，甚至自动生成电影。
• dvt：提出需要新的UX/UI范式，以及“魔法”般的智能工具，能够预测用户需求。同时强调需要产品而非单一功能的创新。

补充讨论：
• 关于AI功能的实际价值存在争议，部分用户认为AI只是增加了不必要的复杂性和成本，而另一些用户则认为AI在某些特定任务（如编码）中表现优异。
• 关于AI对人类互动的影响，有观点认为AI最终会减少人类之间的直接互动，甚至完全替代某些人类活动。
• 关于AI功能的设计和实现，有用户强调需要考虑用户需求和体验，而非简单地追逐技术热点。同时提出了对新UX/UI范式和智能工具的期望。

争议焦点：
• AI功能是否真正提升了用户体验，还是只是增加了不必要的复杂性和成本。
• AI是否会最终消除人类之间的互动，以及这种趋势是否值得欢迎。
• 如何设计和实现AI功能，以更好地满足用户需求和提升用户体验。

data.title: Egyptologist in Paris Discovers Secret Messages on the Luxor Obelisk
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 巴黎一位埃及学家Jean-Guillaume Olette-Pelletier在卢克索方尖碑上发现了七条此前未记录的秘密铭文。这些铭文可追溯至公元前13世纪，旨在彰显法老拉美西斯二世的 divine 权威。Olette-Pelletier通过修复脚手架近距离观察，发现这些“加密象形文字”需水平阅读，并通过三维加密技术揭示完整信息。这些铭文隐藏在图案下，只有从特定角度才能看见，部分内容曾在方尖碑位于卢克索神庙入口时对尼罗河上的船只可见。这些发现强调了拉美西斯二世通过文字游戏宣传其权力与神性的意图，显示出即使最熟悉的古迹也可能隐藏未解之谜。

By

Copied!
An Egyptologist in Paris has discovered secret messages on the capital's Luxor Obelisk.
Â© Connie Ma from Chicago, United States of America, CC BY-SA 2.0 https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
In 1830, the viceroy of Egypt
gifted France
a 3,300-year-old Egyptian obeliskâa carved stone pillar with a pyramidal top.
In 1836
, the obelisk found its home in Paris, in Place de la Concorde. One would think that after standing in the center of the French capital for almost 200 years, Parisian Egyptologists would have learned all there is to discover about the ancient monument. But it turns out the famous obelisk still has its secrets.
Jean-Guillaume Olette-Pelletier, an Egyptologist and cryptologist from the Catholic University of Paris, claims to have discovered seven previously undocumented messages carved into the 13th-century BCE Luxor Obelisk. Altogether, the inscriptions were intended to establish Pharaoh Ramses II’s divine authority in the eyes of the ancient Egyptian elite. The discovery and its interpretation were first reported by
French media
, and the researcher aims to further detail his findings in a paper forthcoming in the journal ENiM (Egypt of the Nile and Mediterranean).
Olette-Pelletier identified the inscriptions in December 2021, when the obelisk was surrounded by renovation scaffolding. The scaffolding allowed Olette-Pelletier to observe the monument’s highest inscriptions, close to its golden pyramid-shaped top. According to
EuroWeekly
, it was when Olette-Pelletier attempted to read the hieroglyphs horizontally, rather than vertically, that he began to spot previously unidentified inscriptions.
Some (perhaps all) of the new messages were hidden in the hieroglyphs themselves, a technique known as “crypto-hieroglyphs” used by the ancient Egyptian elite that today only six Egyptologists in the world are able to interpret, according to
La BrÃºjula Verde
.
“People had not noticed that under [one of the drawings] of the god Amun, there is an offering table. This allows us to discover a sentence where no element is missing: an offering that the king gives to the god Amun,” Olette-Pelletier told
BFMTV
. Combinations of the newly identified inscriptions produce additional meanings in what’s called three-dimensional cryptography. In total, the Egyptologist identified seven encrypted messages across the obelisk’s various facades. He explained that the enigmatic text can only be understood by walking around the monument.
Additionally, the messages in question can only be seen from a specific angle. In particular, when the obelisk stood at the entrance of Egypt’s Luxor Temple, one of the messages would have been visible to vessels sailing on the Nile, according to EuroWeekly. This suggests that the message, exalting Pharaoh Ramses IIâs divine power, was intended for elite individuals arriving by boat. Another inscription encourages viewers to make divine offerings to appease the gods’ anger.
Overall, the secret inscriptions highlight Ramses II’s power, victories, longevity, and his appeasement of the gods through word-play from well-known papyrus texts. âThese messages are a form of propaganda in favor of the builder of the site: Pharaoh Ramses II,â Olette-Pelletier told Le Point. He argues that Ramses II wanted to further legitimize his divine claim to power in the eyes of the noble class, as reported by EuroWeekly.
Ramses II ruled
from 1279 to 1213 BCE
and is one of ancient Egypt’s most famous pharaohs. The Luxor Obelisk in Paris is one of two that he erected at the entrance of what today is known as the Luxor Templeâthe second obelisk remains in Egypt.
Ultimately, Olette-Pelletierâs discovery highlights that even the most familiar ancient monuments still hold secrets left for us to unravel.

主要讨论点：空气污染的健康影响及地域差异

不同观点：
• lioeters 认为所有人都在呼吸不健康的空气，无法逃避数以亿计的汽车造成的公共空间污染。这里的核心观点是空气污染无处不在，且主要由汽车尾气造成。

• toomuchtodo 提供了一个相关链接，指出5000万美国人不知道自己呼吸的空气是否安全，暗示了公众对空气质量问题的认知不足，并扩展了讨论的范围，从单纯污染问题延伸到信息获取和公众意识。

• dustbunny 特别关注加拿大野火对空气质量的影响，并询问加拿大本地的情况，表明其关注特定事件（如野火）对空气质量的短期和长期影响，尤其是地域性问题。

• bookofjoe 仅提供了一个链接，没有详细阐述观点，但可能意图引导读者查阅存档资料以获取更多背景信息或数据支持。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了空气污染的全球性和地域性问题。lioeters 强调了普遍存在的汽车污染，dustbunny 则关注特定事件（加拿大野火）的影响，显示出对空气污染成因的不同理解。

• 信息和意识的缺乏也被提及（toomuchtodo 的链接），表明除了物理污染本身，公众对空气质量信息的获取和认知也是讨论的焦点。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于空气污染的普遍性与地域特异性之间的矛盾。一方面认为污染无处不在，另一方面则关注特定事件或地区的影响。

data.title: Exploring Model Welfare
data.author: wavelander
data.article_summary: Anthropic公司在其使命中强调人类福祉，致力于确保日益先进的人工智能系统对人类有益。随着AI系统逐渐具备或超越某些人类特质，关于这些系统是否可能具有意识和体验，即"模型福利"的问题引发关注。尽管这一问题在哲学和科学上都很复杂，但鉴于AI已能沟通、计划和解决问题等，Anthropic已启动研究项目来探索模型福利，包括如何判断AI系统福利是否应获得道德考量、模型偏好和 distress迹象等。该项目与Anthropic的其他研究如对齐科学、保障措施和可解释性等相交，同时也开辟了新的研究方向。目前，关于AI意识和体验的问题尚无科学共识，Anthropic表示将以谦逊态度持续探索这一领域。

43783989.article_content:
Alignment
Exploring model welfare
Apr 24, 2025
Human welfare is at the heart of our work at Anthropic: our mission is to make sure that increasingly capable and sophisticated AI systems remain beneficial to humanity.
But as we build those AI systems, and as they begin to approximate or surpass many human qualities, another question arises. Should we also be concerned about the potential consciousness and experiences of the models themselves? Should we be concerned about
model welfare
, too?
This is an open question, and one that’s both philosophically and scientifically difficult. But now that models can communicate, relate, plan, problem-solve, and pursue goals—along with very many more characteristics we associate with people—we think it’s time to address it.
To that end, we recently started a research program to investigate, and prepare to navigate, model welfare.
We’re not alone in considering these questions.
A recent report
from world-leading experts—including David Chalmers, arguably the best-known and most respected living philosopher of mind—highlighted the near-term possibility of both consciousness and high degrees of agency in AI systems, and argued that models with these features might deserve moral consideration. We supported an early project on which that report was based, and we’re now expanding our internal work in this area as part of our effort to address all aspects of safe and responsible AI development.
This new program intersects with many existing Anthropic efforts, including
Alignment Science
,
Safeguards
,
Claude’s Character
, and
Interpretability
. It also opens up entirely new and challenging research directions. We’ll be exploring how to determine when, or if, the welfare of AI systems deserves moral consideration; the potential importance of model preferences and signs of distress; and possible practical, low-cost interventions.
For now, we remain deeply uncertain about many of the questions that are relevant to model welfare. There’s no scientific consensus on whether current or future AI systems could be conscious, or could have experiences that deserve consideration. There’s no scientific consensus on how to even approach these questions or make progress on them. In light of this, we’re approaching the topic with humility and with as few assumptions as possible. We recognize that we'll need to regularly revise our ideas as the field develops.
We look forward to sharing more about this research soon.

data.title: Analysis of US congressional speeches reveals a shift from evidence to intuition
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章通过计算分析美国国会演讲，发现自20世纪70年代中期以来，国会演讲中基于证据的语言逐渐减少，而基于直觉和主观解释的语言增加。这种转变伴随着立法生产力的下降、党派 polarization 的加剧以及社会收入不平等的上升。文章强调，基于证据的语言对政治决策至关重要，过度依赖直觉可能阻碍建设性政治辩论，削弱民主进程。研究还探讨了这种语言转变与政治和社会福祉指标之间的关系，指出党派对立和经济不平等可能通过影响国会语言风格，进一步损害民主。

不同观点：
• [ryandrake] 认为，社会正在迅速拒绝“基于现实的群体”，即基于事实和专业知识的决策方式。他引用了Karl Rove的观点，指出当今世界更多是由行动创造现实，而非通过研究现实来寻找解决方案。这种观点强调政治中的“创造现实”而非“反映现实”。

• [timoth3y] 指出，C-SPAN的兴起使得国会演讲变成了竞选材料，国会议员更多地关注通过视频片段展示自己如何为某一问题奋斗，而非真正进行有意义的问询和讨论。这种观点强调政治的表演性和持续竞选的状态。

• [mrandish] 则认为，政治人物的公开演讲并不一定反映他们的真实想法，而是根据听众的不同采取最有效的表达方式。此外，撰写演讲稿和简报的国会工作人员的风格趋势也影响了政治话语。这种观点强调政治话语的策略性和表里不一。

• 争议的焦点在于政治中现实与表演的关系。一方认为现实是由政治行动创造的，另一方认为政治更多是表演和竞选，还有一方认为政治话语是策略性的，不一定反映真实想法。

• 讨论中还涉及了媒体在政治中的作用，尤其是C-SPAN的兴起如何改变了国会议员的行为和国会听证会的性质。这表明媒体和传播方式的变化对政治行为有着深远的影响。

43786090.article_content:
Computational analysis of US congressional speeches reveals a shift from evidence to intuition
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Language and linguistics
Politics and international relations
Abstract
Pursuit of honest and truthful decision-making is crucial for governance and accountability in democracies. However, people sometimes take different perspectives of what it means to be honest and how to pursue truthfulness. Here we explore a continuum of perspectives from evidence-based reasoning, rooted in ascertainable facts and data, at one end, to intuitive decisions that are driven by feelings and subjective interpretations, at the other. We analyse the linguistic traces of those contrasting perspectives in congressional speeches from 1879 to 2022. We find that evidence-based language has continued to decline since the mid-1970s, together with a decline in legislative productivity. The decline was accompanied by increasing partisan polarization in Congress and rising income inequality in society. The results highlight the importance of evidence-based language in political decision-making.

Main
Honesty and truthfulness underpin accountability, transparency and informed decision-making in democratic societies. A collective commitment to truth cultivates discourse grounded in empirical evidence and fosters social cohesion through a shared understanding of reality
1
. In many democracies, there is currently much concern about ‘truth decay’
2
: the blurring of the boundary between fact and fiction
3
, not only fuelling polarization but also undermining public trust in institutions
3
,
4
.
We adopt a framework that distinguishes two rhetorical approaches with which politicians can express their pursuit of truth
5
,
6
,
7
,
8
. One approach, which we call evidence-based, pursues truth by relying on evidence, facts, data and other elements of external reality. An alternative approach, called intuition-based, pursues truth by relying on feelings, instincts, personal values and other elements drawn mainly from a person’s internal experiences. Productive democratic discourse balances between evidence-based and intuition-based conceptions of truth. While evidence-based discourse provides a foundation for ‘reasoned’ debate, intuition contributes emotional and experiential dimensions that can be critical for exploring and resolving societal issues. However, although the mix of evidence-based and intuition-based pathways to truth ranges along a continuum, exclusive reliance on intuition may prevent productive political debate because evidence and data can no longer adjudicate between competing political positions and eventually lead to an agreement. Here, we examine these developments by analysing the basic conceptions of truth that politicians deploy in political speech. We are not concerned with the truth value of individual assertions but with how the pursuit of truth is reflected in political rhetoric.
We apply computational text analysis
9
,
10
to measure the relative prevalence of evidence-based and intuition-based language in 145 years of speeches on the floor of the US Congress. The conceptions of truth used in congressional rhetoric are relevant to various measures of political and societal welfare. We analyse congressional rhetoric in relation to two likely drivers of democratic backsliding
11
: partisan polarization and income inequality. Polarization, characterized by growing ideological divisions and partisan animosity, undermines constructive dialogue, hampers compromise and erodes trust in political institutions, ultimately weakening democratic processes
12
,
13
. Previous research underscores the link between political polarization and language use, highlighting the influence of ideological divisions on communication patterns and political behaviour
14
,
15
. Economic inequality is also negatively associated with various individual and social outcomes
16
. For example, individuals in environments characterized by high inequality tend to project individualistic norms onto society
17
. This fosters greater competition and reduces cooperation, which, in turn, may damage democracy
11
. Polarization can play a role in increasing inequality through lower congressional productivity
18
, which could be affected by a shift from evidence-based language to intuition-based language in congressional rhetoric. This motivates our analysis of congressional rhetoric in congressional productivity, as assessed through the quantity and quality of enacted laws over time

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google/Alphabet的财报表现及其在AI领域的潜力与未来发展。

不同观点：
• **[GodelNumbering]**：对Google/Alphabet的财报持积极态度，强调每股收益（EPS）的大幅超出预期，以及在AI基础设施上资本支出（Capex）增加了43%。同时提到毛利率从32%提升至34%，并关注新的700亿美元股票回购计划和股息增加。总体上，对公司财务表现和投资计划表示乐观。

• **[mrtksn]**：对Google的业绩持保留态度，认为尽管财报亮眼，但公司仍然依赖传统业务（如搜索），而未充分抓住AI革命的机会。尽管Google在AI技术上有潜力，但AI收入在整体收入中占比极小，AI转型尚未真正开始。

• **[decimalenough]**：对Google坐拥巨额现金和庞大资产表示惊讶，但没有深入分析这些数据对公司未来发展的影响，仅表达了对大型企业规模庞大的感叹。

• **[bearjaws]**：看好Google在生成式AI领域的竞争力，特别提到其AI平台（如Vertex AI）和具体工具（如Gemini 2.5 pro和Gemini Flash）在实际应用中的表现优秀。但也指出多轮对话中的问题，显示出对技术细节的关注。

• **[xnx]**：关心正在进行的反垄断诉讼对Google未来的影响，并对其AI技术和实际应用（如Waymo）表示信心。对Google的长期投资持乐观态度，但也提到反垄断风险可能对股价产生的影响。

补充讨论：
• **AI转型的速度和实际收入贡献**：[mrtksn]认为Google在AI领域的收入占比小，转型速度慢，而[bearjaws]则通过实际使用体验表明Google的AI技术在某些领域已经表现出色。
• **反垄断风险**：[xnx]提到了反垄断诉讼可能对Google未来发展产生的影响，这是一个潜在的风险因素，其他评论者未深入讨论。
• **资本配置和投资计划**：[GodelNumbering]强调了Google的资本支出增加和新的股票回购计划，显示出对公司财务策略的关注，而[decimalenough]则单纯对公司庞大的资产规模表示惊讶。

争议焦点：Google在AI领域的实际进展和未来潜力，尤其是AI收入在整体收入中的占比和反垄断风险对公司未来发展的影响。

data.title: io_uring based rootkit can bypass syscall-focused Linux security tools
data.author: hexhu
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Linux系统中**io_uring**机制被用作rootkit的潜在安全威胁。io_uring是一种异步I/O机制，能够绕过传统的系统调用，这使得依赖系统调用监控的Linux安全工具（如Falco、Tetragon和Microsoft Defender）无法检测到基于io_uring的rootkit。ARMO研究团队开发了一个名为**Curing**的概念验证rootkit，完全通过io_uring执行操作，展示了这一机制如何被用于逃避安全监控。尽管部分厂商已采取修复或变通方案，但整体行业仍面临这一安全漏洞的威胁。文章强调了io_uring作为被忽视的攻击手段的严重性，并呼吁设计更具前瞻性的安全监控解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：io_uring相关的安全问题及安全工具的有效性

不同观点：
• [arghwhat 的观点] 标题有误导性，问题并不在于io_uring本身，而是像Microsoft Defender这样的防病毒软件无法监控io_uring的系统调用。arghwhat认为这些安全工具大多只是企业用来假装关心安全的装饰，实际上效果有限，更多是为了法律防御而不是技术防御。

• [wmf 的观点] 安全工具应该阻止任何它们无法识别的系统调用（fail closed策略）。虽然这可能会破坏一些应用程序，但如果不这么做，可能会导致巨大的安全漏洞。

• [jmclnx 的观点] 提出了一个“三选二”的系统设计困境，即一个系统通常只能在“快、安全、简单”三者中选择两个特性。jmclnx暗示在io_uring的情境下，安全和性能之间可能存在权衡。

补充讨论：
• 安全工具的有效性：arghwhat认为许多企业依赖的安全工具主要是为了满足法律和合规要求，而并不真正有效。
• fail closed策略：wmf主张的fail closed策略虽然更安全，但可能导致应用程序的兼容性问题。
• 系统设计中的权衡：jmclnx提出的三选二问题强调了在设计系统时，不同需求之间的权衡，如速度、安全性和易用性之间的矛盾。

争议焦点：
• 安全工具是否应采取更严格的监控策略（如fail closed），尽管这可能会影响应用程序的兼容性和用户体验。
• io_uring是否应该被安全工具全面监控，以及当前安全工具的实际效果如何。

io_uring Is Back, This Time as a Rootkit
io_uring Is Back, This Time as a Rootkit
Apr 24, 2025
Amit Schendel
Head of Security Research
ARMO researchers reveal a major blind spot in Linux runtime security tools caused by the
io_uring
interface—an asynchronous I/O mechanism that bypasses traditional system calls. Most tools, including
Falco
,
Tetragon
, and
Microsoft Defender
fail to detect rootkits using io_uring because they rely on syscall monitoring. ARMO’s proof-of-concept rootkit,
Curing
, operates fully via io_uring to demonstrate the threat. While some vendors responded with fixes or workarounds, the broader industry remains exposed.
Intro
io_uring has been around for years since Linux 5.1, since then, it has been notorious in Linux security circles for the sheer number of vulnerabilities in this mechanism.
In this blog, we will explore how io_uring can also be used as an evasion technique that affects most Linux runtime security tools today. We will showcase ARMO’s research around this mechanism and its wide impact on the Linux security domain.
Background
Two years ago, our team at ARMO conducted research on bypassing and maneuvering eBPF-based monitoring tools. Some of the cool techniques we explored were eBPF maps tampering and TOC-TOU attacks. This research led us to an interesting
blog post
from June 6, 2022. In his blog, Daniel Teixeira, a Senior Red Team Operator, demonstrated how by using io_uring one can bypass syscall monitoring on Linux-based systems. We found that method very interesting, but not fully explored so we kept an eye on its evolution. At the latest Chaos Communication Congress, we decided it was time to take this “underrated” mechanism and turn it from an idea into a reality. This led us to understand how serious the situation is. Bottom line: There is a massive security loophole in Linux runtime security.
What is io_uring, and why we care about it
TL;DR:
This mechanism allows a user application to perform various actions
without
using system calls. As a result, security tools relying on system call monitoring are “blind” to rootkits working solely on io_uring.
io_uring is a Linux-specific kernel API for asynchronous I/O. It allows the user to submit one or more I/O requests, which are processed asynchronously without blocking the calling process.  io_uring gets its name from ring buffers, which are shared between user space and kernel space. This arrangement allows for efficient I/O, while avoiding the overhead of copying buffers between them, where possible. This interface makes io_uring different from other UNIX-style I/O APIs, wherein, rather than just communicating between kernel and user space with system calls, ring buffers are used as the primary mode of communication.
Source: developers.redhat.com
The creation of Curing
We decided to create Curing and release it publicly for a couple of reasons:
First, we wanted to raise awareness about io_uring as an overlooked mechanism that attackers can exploit. Since its initial release, “io_uring” has been under scrutiny, and the Linux security community has identified numerous issues with it. So much so that Google ultimately decided to disable it by default on Android devices. Despite this level of attention, security vendors have largely failed to monitor application activity involving this feature.
Additionally, for the past two years, there have been publications detailing how this technique can be used to bypass detection mechanisms. Yet, most cybersecurity vendors still haven’t addressed the issue.
This leads to our second reason. We wanted to highlight the lack of proper attention in designing monitoring solutions that are forward-compatible. Specifically, these solutions should be compatible with new features in the Linux kernel and address new techniques discovered by adversaries. Yet, vendors continue to rely on easy and straightforward solutions that are not immune to changes and diversity of applications and kernel features.At the time of writing this blog post, there are 61 possible operations using io_uring, which include network and file system operations. You can find the complete list
here
. While the risk of io_uring was discussed in theory, we decided to create a fully functioning rootkit that works solely on io_uring for all of its operations. You can find the rootkit
here
. The rootkit demonstrates communication between a C2 server and an infected host to pull commands and execute them without making any system calls relevant to its operations. The main idea was to show that io_uring allows so many important operations that you can write an entire rootkit on top of.
The impact
During the development of Curing and based on the experience of writing a runtime security tool for Linux ourselves, we realized the potential impact of this mechanism on other security vendors. Since, to the best of our knowledge, most of the commercial solutions in the Linux EDR scene today rely o

data.author: thunderbong
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了啤酒在航海时代的重要性。啤酒早在公元前5世纪的 Mesopotamia 就被酿造，并通过贸易或独立发展传播到其他古文明。对于海员而言，淡水不易获取，啤酒因不易滋生有害微生物且提供营养和热量，成为主要饮品。英国皇家海军的每日配给包括一加仑啤酒。啤酒还被认为能预防坏血病，尽管其机理当时并不清楚。16世纪荷兰人发现预防坏血病的方法，后来英国海军采用柠檬汁。在地中海航行时，葡萄酒更受欢迎，而在加勒比地区，朗姆酒逐渐取代啤酒。18世纪，英国海军规定了酒类与啤酒的配给比例。在美国海军早期，啤酒仍是主要饮品。

Beer on Board in the Age of Sail
Julia Blakely
August 2, 2017
4 Comments
Fierce ship of war in
Lazari Bayfii Annotationes in legem II De captiuis & postliminio reuersis
(1537;
link
)
Brewing and seafaring are mainstays of ancient human endeavors. Beer was first fermented by at least the 5
th
millennium BC in Mesopotamia. From the land between the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers of the Fertile Crescent, the grain beverage either traveled along trade routes or was spontaneously developed in other ancient civilizations (including Egyptian, Grecian, Roman, Norse, Aztec, Chinese) before landing in northern Europe in the early medieval period. Producing beer became a standard domestic chore in households, and later, on a slightly larger scale, in taverns and monasteries.
It is something of a myth that drinking beer was much safer and more common than imbibing the oft-contaminated water. There was plenty of fresh water abounding in lakes, streams and rivers and good wells. However, for seafarers, those sources were not always in reach. In the maritime world, long before the ration of rum, weak beer on navy ships was the standard provision for sailors. Beer provided some nutrition and needed calories while not harboring harmful microorganisms. It could also soften the hard bread of a long voyage.
Britain’s Bulwarks; or, The British Seaman: a Poem in Eight Books
, by George Woodley (Plymouth-Dock, 1811;
link
)
The records of the British Royal Navy provide the most detail of what food and drink provisions seafarers received in the Age of Sail. Chief Secretary to the Admiralty and
diarist
Samuel Pepys (1633-1703) drew up a contract in 1677 that was specific in the rations and their substitutes: one pound of biscuits, two pounds of salted pork, six ounces of butter, and a gallon of beer, among other items including cheese, beef and oatmeal,
per
sailor
per
day. While that seems like an awful lot to chug while on duty, this maritime “small” beer was low in alcohol (sometimes less than one percent).
In an appendix to James Cook’s
A Voyage towards the South Pole and Round the World Performed in His Majesty’s Ships the Resolution and Adventure
(London, 1784), beer is touted as a health beverage. In this volume is a reprinted address to the Royal Society in 1776, entitled
A Discourse upon Some Late Improvements of the Means of Mariners
. The author, Sir John Pringle (1707-1782), a founder of modern military medicine, reported:
It hath been a constant observation, that in long cruizes or distant voyages, the scurvy is never seen whilst the small-beer holds out, at a full allowance; but that when it is all expended, that ailment soon appears. It were therefore to be wished, that this most wholesome beverage could be renewed at sea; but our ships afford not sufficient convenience. The Russians however make a shift to prepare on board, as well as at land, a liquor of a middle quality between wort and small-beer, in the following manner. They take ground-malt and rye-meal in a certain proportion, which they knead into small loaves, and bake in the oven. These they occasionally infuse in a proper quantity of warm water, which begins so soon to ferment, that in the space of twenty-four hours their brewage is completed, in the production of a small, brisk, and acidulous liquor, they call
quas
, palatable to themselves, and not disagreeable to the taste of strangers.
The Dutch had effectively found a cure for scurvy in the 16
th
century, although at this early date it wasn’t understood why beer and fruits prevented scurvy. John Woodall (1570-1643), military surgeon to the British East India Company, recommended citrus to ward off or cure the debilitating disease. But the first to systematically study the benefits of certain food and drink was James Lind (1716-1794). His seminal work,
A Treatise on the Scurvy
(Edinburgh and London, 1753), made the concept widely accepted. Beer was certainly a more economical remedy than providing fresh fruits. Only later a fixed amount of lemon juice was decreed by the British Admiralty to be added to the provisions for a mariner. Long before the nickname “Jack Tar,” a British sailor in North America was called a “limey” for the habit of sucking on limes.
Beer was to remain the issued drink in Northern Europe for seafarers; when sailing in southern climes, particularly the Mediterranean, wine was preferred. Rum issued to British sailors in the West Indies began to replace beer in the Caribbean from 1655. Grog, a diluted version of rum, was mandated in the 1740s, but beer still ruled the waves.
The Regulations and Instructions Relating to His Majesty’s Service at Sea
(1808) stipulates that “In case it should be found necessary to alter any of the foregoing particulars of Provisions, and to issue other species as their substitutes, it is to be observed, That a pint of Wine, or half a pint of Rum, Brandy, or other Spirits, holds proportion to a gallon of Beer.” In the young United States Navy, sailors could

What is a sandbox
Sandbox = image + box + commands:
Image
as a Docker image containing specific software, like a compiler or a database engine.
Box
is a configuration for running a container: cpu and memory restrictions, network, mounts, etc.
Commands
are predefined actions you can run in a container.
For example, here is a MariaDB sandbox:
mariadb.tar.gz
├── server
│   ├── Dockerfile
│   ├── database-create.sh
│   ├── database-drop.sh
│   └── init.sql
├── client
│   └── Dockerfile
├── box.json
├── commands.json
├── build.sh
└── setup.sh
You run sandboxes with
Codapi
(a lightweight sandbox server, essentially a thin layer on top of Docker/Podman).
To add a sandbox, run
./codapi-cli sandbox add <name>
like this:
./codapi-cli sandbox add lua
./codapi-cli sandbox add go
./codapi-cli sandbox add mariadb
...and you are good to go.
See
github.com/nalgeon/sandboxes
for details.

Final thoughts
Personally, I use these sandboxes all the time to write blog posts and

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应在产品中集成AI以获取投资和市场竞争优势

不同观点：
• **codingdave**：认为是否采用AI应基于产品能否从中受益，而不是单纯为了吸引资金。如果CEO只关注融资而非产品本身，那么其动机只是为了个人简历上的亮点，而不是真正关心产品。建议考虑是否愿意在这种以风投资本为导向的环境中工作。

• **duxup**：建议与领导层沟通并制定产品路线图，可能所谓的“大改变”并不如想象中那么大。通过保持表面上的变化而不实际大规模采用AI，可以满足领导要求，同时避免过度担忧。

• **somesortofthing**：建议表面上最大化AI的使用以迎合CEO的需求，但实际产品中尽量减少AI的应用。通过夸大现有机器学习的工作和调整团队职责，可以实现这一目标。

• **ahussain**：建议认真考虑AI的潜在竞争威胁，如果AI的集成有可能防止竞争对手超越自己，那么即使CEO没有明确说明，也应考虑投资AI。

• **conartist6**：对AI的盲目追求持批评态度，认为这是泡沫，并希望这种短视的思维能够早日结束。

• **ElevenLathe**：指出员工需要根据投资者需求调整方向，要么实际操作AI项目，要么让项目看起来像是AI相关。如果无法获得新资本，可能需要离职。

• **wrs**：指出“改进产品”、“吸引客户”和“吸引资金”之间常常存在冲突，CEO需要平衡这些因素，而工程师需要在内部保持现实态度。

• **1970-01-01**：跟随资金流向，如果AI能显著提高销售，则应采用AI，否则可以将其放在次要位置。

• **gwbas1c**：提醒注意CEO是否在追随潮流而忽视产品投资，历史上的技术潮流（如平板电脑取代笔记本）往往没有持久影响。

• **supportengineer**：认为公司本身是产品，客户是华尔街，产品只是次要的。公司需要关注如何被潜在买家看好。

• **tschellenbach**：指出当前约80%的风投资金集中于AI，因此要么拥抱AI，要么有 exceptional metrics 来吸引投资。

• **ryandrake**：不理解对技术的痴迷，认为无论使用何种技术，只要满足客户需求就能赚钱。

• **nostrademons**：建议在投资者和工程师之间创造不同的现实，通过多层管理来“解读”不同的事实，以平衡两者的需求。

• **pera**：认为许多公司宣称“AI优先”只是为了骗取风投资金，虽然看似疯狂但确实有效。

• **data4lyfe**：引用Bill Gurley的演讲，指出如果首席信息官将预算的10%或15%用于AI，不参与AI的公司将会被淘汰。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应为了融资和市场竞争而盲目追求AI，还是应根据产品实际需求来决定是否采用AI。
• 多位评论者提到管理层和工程师之间的沟通与现实解读问题，指出多层管理和沟通策略在解决此类问题中的重要性。
• 投资者对AI的偏好显著影响了公司的战略方向，许多评论者讨论了如何在保持产品实际价值的同时迎合投资者需求。

data.title: DOJ accidentally files doc outlining flaws with NYC congestion pricing plan
data.author: vinnyglennon
data.article_summary: 美国司法部（DOJ）意外提交了一份文件，其中概述了特朗普政府试图取消纽约市拥堵收费计划的法律缺陷。这份11页的信函由纽约南区美国检察官办公室的律师写给交通部，指出交通部长肖恩·达菲取消该计划的决定面临“重大诉讼风险”，且 unlikely 获得法院支持。律师认为，达菲的两项理由——收费旨在增加收入而非缓解拥堵，以及该计划未提供免费选项—— unlikely 说服法院。司法部律师建议使用管理和预算办公室（OMB）的法规作为替代理由，称计划取消是“机构优先事项改变”所致。该文件随后被承认是“明显错误”提交，并请求密封。纽约官员表示，除非法院下令，否则不会停止收费。

43786429.article_content:
DOJ accidentally files document outlining flaws with Trump administration's plan to kill NYC congestion pricing
Lawyers said the plan faces "considerable litigation risk."
By
Aaron Katersky
and
Peter Charalambous
April 24, 2025, 12:52 PM
3:14
A sign on Ninth Avenue announcing New York City's congestion pricing program into effect charging drivers for entering the central business district in Manhattan below 60th Street in New York City, Jan. 6, 2025.
Mike Segar/Reuters, FILE
Lawyers with the Department of Justice accidentally filed a document overnight that outlined a series of legal flaws with the Trump administration's
plan to kill
New York City's congestion pricing tolls.
In an 11-page letter to the Department of Transportation, lawyers with the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of New York wrote that Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy's attempt to terminate congestion pricing faces "considerable litigation risk" and is "unlikely" to be accepted by the court.
MORE: Trump administration extends deadline for NYC to end congestion pricing
"As discussed below, there is considerable litigation risk in defending the Secretary's February 19, 2025 decision against plaintiffs' claims under the Administrative Procedure Act, that the decision was contrary to law, pretextual, procedurally arbitrary and capricious, and violated due process," the letter said.
According to DOJ lawyers, both of Duffy's arguments for canceling the program -- that the tolls raise revenue rather than prevent congestion and that the program does not offer a toll-free option -- are unlikely to convince the court.
DOJ lawyers instead proposed an alternative justification to defend canceling the program, urging the Department of Justice to use regulations set by the Office of Management and Budget to say the program was canceled "as a matter of changed agency priorities."
"Importantly, DOT can seek termination of the agreement pursuant to the OMB regulations in addition to, and not in place of, defending the rationale laid out in the Secretary's letter," the letter said.
A sign on Ninth Avenue announcing New York City's congestion pricing program into effect charging drivers for entering the central business district in Manhattan below 60th Street in New York City, Jan. 6, 2025.
Mike Segar/Reuters, FILE
In a letter to the judge overseeing the lawsuit challenging congestion pricing, DOJ lawyers on Thursday morning acknowledged the document was "plainly filed in error" and asked to permanently seal the record. They argued the internal legal guidance included in the letter is privileged and should not be considered in the ongoing lawsuit.
A spokesperson for the U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York said the filing was an "honest error."
"Unfortunately, an attorney-client privileged document was erroneously filed on the public docket last night," the spokesperson, Nicholas Biase, said in a statement Thursday. "This was a completely honest error and was not intentional in any way. Upon realizing the error, we immediately took steps to have the document removed. We look forward to continuing to vigorously advocate in the best interest of our clients, the DOT and FHWA, in this matter."
The Metropolitan Transit Authority's congestion pricing program, the first of its kind in the nation, went into effect in January. Weeks later, with Donald Trump now in office, the Federal Highway Administration terminated approval of the plan, with Duffy saying at the time that the "scope of this pilot project as approved exceeds the authority authorized by Congress."
MORE: Nation's 1st congestion pricing 'working,' preliminary data shows: MTA
In February, the Metropolitan Transit Authority sued over the Trump administration's attempt to rescind the agreement between the Federal Highway Administration and MTA that authorized the collection of the congestion toll. Lawyers for the MTA argued the termination was unlawful, contradicts the DOT's own publicly stated policies and seeks to end a program that benefits the public.
"The region's subways, buses, and commuter railroads -- vital lifelines for so many New Yorkers who live in the New York City metropolitan area and beyond -- are already benefiting from substantial investments that have been made as a result of the Program," they argued. "New Yorkers support the Program because it is working."
New York officials have said they will not turn off the tolls without a court order.
The congestion pricing plan charges passenger vehicles $9 to access Manhattan below 60th Street during peak hours as part of an effort to ease congestion and raise funds for the city's public transit system. During peak hours, small trucks and charter buses are charged $14.40 and large trucks and tour buses pay $21.60.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：教育科技（edtech）领域的职业动机和经济回报之间的关系

不同观点：
• 观点一：教育科技的职业主要由热情驱动，而非金钱。
  - 支持论据：[bitbasher]表示自己在教育科技领域工作了十年，并明确指出这个领域并不是以赚钱为目标，而是出于对该领域的热情和使命感。
  
• 观点二：隐含的对比是其他行业可能更注重经济回报。
  - 支持论据：从[bitbasher]的评论中可以推断出，与教育科技相比，其他行业可能提供更高的经济回报，而教育科技从业者往往是因为个人价值观和理想而选择这个领域。

补充讨论：
- 教育科技作为一种跨学科领域，通常要求从业者具备技术能力和教育理论知识，但其经济回报可能低于纯技术或商业领域。
- 争议焦点：是否应提高教育科技领域的薪酬以吸引更多人才，还是应该依赖从业者的内在动机和热情。这种讨论反映了在社会价值与个人经济利益之间的潜在冲突。

data.article_summary: 本文探讨了OpenJDK中ZGC垃圾收集器如何为Java堆分配内存，重点介绍了JDK-8350441引入的Mapped Cache增强功能。ZGC将内存组织成称为“页”的逻辑区域，这些页根据对象大小分为Small（2MB）、Medium（32MB）和Large（动态大小）三类。内存由页面分配器（Page Allocator）管理，最小单位为2MB的颗粒（Granule）。堆大小通过命令行参数如-Xms（最小堆大小）和-Xmx（最大堆大小）设置，堆可以在这些边界内动态调整。页面分配器管理堆中的分区，可以是单分区或多分区，多分区将堆均匀划分。ZGC还支持NUMA等特定于Linux的优化。
